title: The Football Match
author: Barashada Ingiriisiga
description: Two friends on a local youth soccer team learn that playing together matters more than winning or losing, in one important match that changes how they see the game.

chapters.title: The Big Match
chapters.text:
Sam and Ali were best friends. They played football for the Riverside youth team. Every Tuesday and Thursday, they went to the park after school. They practiced passing, shooting, and running with the ball. Sam was a good player, but he was quiet. Ali was loud and always smiled. They were different, but they were a great team.

One Tuesday afternoon, their coach, Mr. Green, called all the players together. He had a big smile on his face. "Listen, everyone," he said. "I have important news. The final match is on Saturday. We play against the City boys. It is the biggest match of the year."

The players shouted and clapped. Ali jumped in the air. "Yes! We can win!" he cried. Sam smiled too, but his stomach felt strange.

All week, the team practiced hard. On Wednesday, they ran around the park five times. On Thursday, they did passing drills. Mr. Green shouted, "Pass the ball! Move! Shoot!" The players worked very hard.

Ali played very well. He scored three goals in the practice. He laughed and said, "Sam, we are going to win on Saturday. I know it."

Sam tried to smile. "Yes, maybe," he said. But inside, he felt worried. What if he made a mistake? What if he lost the ball? What if the City boys were too fast?

On Thursday night, Sam talked to his mother. "Mum, I am scared about the match," he said. "What if I do something wrong?"

His mother put her hand on his head. "Sam, you practice hard. You are a good player. Just do your best. That is enough."

Sam nodded, but the worry did not go away.

Friday came. The team had a short practice. Mr. Green said, "Rest today. Eat well. Sleep well. The match is tomorrow."

That night, Sam went to bed at nine o'clock. He closed his eyes. But he could not sleep. He thought about the match. He thought about the big crowd. He thought about the City boys. They were tall and strong. They had won many matches this year.

Sam turned in his bed. He looked at the clock. Ten o'clock. Eleven o'clock. Still awake. Outside, the wind made a soft sound. His football boots sat on the floor next to his bed. They looked ready for the match.

Sam closed his eyes again. He remembered his mother's words. "Just do your best." He took a deep breath. Slowly, slowly, his eyes became heavy.

In the next room, Ali was also in bed. But Ali was not worried. He smiled in the dark. Saturday was coming. He was ready.

chapters.title: The Match
chapters.text:
On Saturday morning, the sun was bright and the sky was blue. Sam and Ali walked to the football field together. Sam did not say much. He thought about the match and his stomach felt strange. Ali put his hand on Sam's shoulder. "Today is our day," Ali said. "Do not worry."

The Riverside team wore their red shirts. The other team, the Tigers, wore yellow. Many parents and friends sat near the field. The coach called the players together. "Remember what we practiced," he said. "Pass the ball. Help each other. Play as one team."

The referee blew his whistle. The match started. Sam ran fast. He watched the ball. He did not think about mistakes. He only thought about the game.

In the first ten minutes, Riverside played very well. They passed the ball and moved together. Then Ali got the ball near the goal. He saw Sam on the left. He passed the ball to Sam. Sam controlled it with his foot. He looked at the goal. He kicked the ball hard. It went into the net! The crowd shouted and clapped. Sam smiled. His friends ran to him. "Great goal!" Ali said.

But the Tigers did not stop. They played stronger after that. In the twenty-fifth minute, a Tiger player kicked the ball. It went past the goalkeeper. The score was one - one.

In the second half, the match was fast. Both teams wanted to win. Then Sam got the ball near his own goal. A Tiger player ran to him. Sam tried to pass the ball, but he was too slow. The Tiger player took the ball and kicked it into the goal. The Tigers were winning, two - one.

Ali was very angry. He shouted at Sam. "Why did you do that? What were you thinking?" Sam looked down. His face was red. He did not say anything. He felt very sad. He wanted to leave the field.

The coach called them together. He looked at Ali and then at Sam. "Stop," he said. "This is a team. One mistake is not one player's mistake. We win together and we lose together. Listen to me. We still have time. We must work together."

Sam looked at the coach. Then he looked at Ali. Ali felt sorry for his angry words. "I am sorry, Sam," Ali said softly. "Let us play together."

They played hard for the last ten minutes. In the last minute, Ali scored a goal for Riverside. The score was two - two. The referee blew his whistle. The match was a draw.

The players were tired, but they smiled. They did not win, but they did not lose. Sam learned something important that day. Football is not about one player. It is about the team.

chapters.title: After the Whistle
chapters.text:
After the final whistle, the players walked off the field. Their heads were down. They felt sad. The match ended in a draw. Sam looked at the ground. He thought about his mistake. He made a bad pass in the second half. That mistake gave the other team a goal. Ali came to Sam. "Don't be sad," Ali said. "We played well."

The coach called the team together. He smiled at them. "Listen," he said. "You played a good match. You ran fast. You passed the ball well. You worked as a team. I am proud of you." The players listened. Some of them still felt sad. The coach continued. "A draw is not a loss. You learned a lot today. You learned to never give up. That is important."

Sam and Ali sat on the grass. Sam said, "I made a big mistake. I feel bad." Ali put his hand on Sam's shoulder. "Everyone makes mistakes," Ali said. "You are a good player. We are a team. We win together and we lose together. But a draw is not losing. It is a chance to do better." Sam looked at Ali. "You are right," he said. "Winning is not everything. Playing well and having fun is important too."

Then the other team came over. They wanted to shake hands. Sam and Ali stood up. They shook hands with the other players. "Good game," everyone said. The other team's captain smiled. "You played very well," he said to Sam. Sam felt a little better.

After that, Ali had an idea. "Let's practice together next week," he said to the other team. "We can get better." The other team's captain nodded. "Yes, let's do it. We can practice together on Tuesday." Sam smiled. "That is a great idea," he said.

The team walked off the field together. They were not sad anymore. They were proud. They played a hard match. They learned something. They made new friends. Sam looked at Ali. "Thank you," he said. "You are a good friend." Ali smiled. "We are a good team," he said.

questions.question: Why did Sam feel sad after the match?
options: Because his team lost the match
Because he made a bad pass that led to a goal
Because Ali was angry with him
Because the coach was unhappy
questions.explanation: The text says: 'He made a bad pass in the second half. That mistake gave the other team a goal.'

questions.question: What does the word 'draw' mean in this chapter?
options: A game where both teams score the same number of goals
A game where one team wins easily
A game that is stopped early
A game where no one plays well
questions.explanation: The match ended in a draw, and the coach says 'A draw is not a loss.' This means it is a tie, not a win or loss.

questions.question: What did the coach say to the team after the match?
options: He said they played badly and needed to practice more
He said they played a good match and he was proud of them
He said that Sam should not play in the next game
He said that a draw is the same as losing
questions.explanation: The coach said: 'You played a good match... I am proud of you.'

questions.question: What does the phrase 'shake hands' mean in this chapter?
options: To show anger by hitting hands
To greet or say goodbye by holding and moving hands
To practice playing with hands
To ask for the ball
questions.explanation: The other team came over to shake hands. This is a friendly gesture to show respect after a game.
